en: Seeking the Aid of Great Men

kurals.tr: Aranarindhu Mooththa Arivutaiyaar Kenmai / Thiranarindhu Therndhu Kolal
kurals.m: Let (a king) ponder well its value, and secure the friendship of men of virtue and of mature knowledge

kurals.tr: Utranoi Neekki Uraaamai Murkaakkum / Petriyaarp Penik Kolal
kurals.m: Let (a king) procure and kindly care for men who can overcome difficulties when they occur, and guard against them before they happen

kurals.tr: Ariyavatru Lellaam Aridhe Periyaaraip / Penith Thamaraak Kolal
kurals.m: To cherish great men and make them his own, is the most difficult of all difficult things

kurals.tr: Thammir Periyaar Thamaraa Ozhukudhal / Vanmaiyu Lellaan Thalai
kurals.m: So to act as to make those men, his own, who are greater than himself is of all powers the highest

kurals.tr: Soozhvaarkan Naaka Ozhukalaan Mannavan / Soozhvaaraik Soozhndhu Kolal
kurals.m: As a king must use his ministers as eyes (in managing his kingdom), let him well examine their character and qualifications before he engages them

kurals.tr: Thakkaa Rinaththanaaith Thaanozhuka Vallaanaich / Chetraar Seyakkitandha Thil
kurals.m: There will be nothing left for enemies to do, against him who has the power of acting (so as to secure) the fellowship of worthy men

kurals.tr: Itikkun Thunaiyaarai Yaalvarai Yaare / Ketukkun Thakaimai Yavar
kurals.m: Who are great enough to destroy him who has servants that have power to rebuke him ?

kurals.tr: Itippaarai Illaadha Emaraa Mannan / Ketuppaa Rilaanung Ketum
kurals.m: The king, who is without the guard of men who can rebuke him, will perish, even though there be no one to destroy him

kurals.tr: Mudhalilaarkku Oodhiya Millai Madhalaiyaanjjch / Aarpilaark Killai Nilai
kurals.m: There can be no gain to those who have no capital; and in like manner there can be no permanence to

kurals.tr: Pallaar Pakai Kolalir Paththatuththa / Theemaiththe Nallaar Thotarkai Vital
kurals.m: It is tenfold more injurious to abandon the friendship of the good, than to incur the hatred of the many
